title: Alice Garnett
gist: An author index page (not an article) for Alice Garnett, a 26-year-old London writer with 38 pieces in Prospect's Lives column; the headline set is a consumer-behaviour dataset on Gen Z — being made redundant twice in her twenties, logging off for an 'analogue year', refusing an AI friend, workwear cycles, and a call for Gen Z to save the pub.

themes.theme: Gen Z digital retreat and AI resistance

insights.claim: A Gen Z columnist writes explicitly that she does not want an AI friend, and separately that her cohort is logging off and embracing an 'analogue year', indicating consumer resistance to AI companion products among the youngest adult demographic.
insights.speaker: Prospect Magazine
insights.so_what: AI-companion TAM assumptions that rest on young users may be overstated; watch churn and stated aversion in the 18-30 cohort.
insights.quote: I don’t want an AI friend!
insights.locator: Lives / I don’t want an AI friend!

insights.claim: The same columnist defends not replying to texts, framing reduced digital responsiveness as a norm rather than rudeness among younger users.
insights.speaker: Prospect Magazine
insights.so_what: Falling messaging responsiveness among young users pressures engagement metrics for communications and social platforms.
insights.quote: Don’t be offended when I don’t text you back
insights.locator: Lives / Don’t be offended when I don’t text you back

insights.claim: A 26-year-old writer reports having been made redundant twice in her twenties, and separately that her generation lives with the threat of annihilation as prior generations did — a precarity-normalisation frame among young UK professionals.
insights.speaker: Prospect Magazine
insights.so_what: Repeated early-career redundancy suppresses young-adult savings, housing formation and discretionary spend — a structural drag on UK consumer categories.
insights.quote: Young life: I have been made redundant for the second time in my twenties
insights.locator: Lives / Young life: I have been made redundant

insights.claim: The column argues it is up to Gen Z to save Britain's pubs, implicitly conceding that the sector's survival now depends on a cohort that drinks and socialises differently.
insights.speaker: Prospect Magazine
insights.so_what: UK pub and on-trade demand hinges on converting a cohort with weaker drinking habits — a persistent structural headwind for hospitality.
insights.quote: It’s up to Gen Z to save our pubs
insights.locator: Lives / It’s up to Gen Z to save our pubs

insights.claim: Gen Z women are advised to ditch the 'office siren' look, showing how fast the young-professional workwear aesthetic cycle turns in UK commentary.
insights.speaker: Prospect Magazine
insights.so_what: Rapid micro-trend turnover in young-adult fashion keeps inventory risk high for apparel retailers chasing viral aesthetics.
insights.quote: Why gen Z women should ditch the ‘office siren’ look
